findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer requires conditional inclusion methods to be named `include_<attribute>?` (with a trailing question mark). Because `def include_website_name` is missing `?`, AMS ignores it and always includes `website_name` in the serialized JSON (as `nil` when no website is set). Furthermore, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden for TL0 users when viewed by anonymous users (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), and `untrusted_attributes` automatically defines `include_<attr>?` for every attribute passed to it. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the manual `include_website_name` method) fixes both the missing `?` and the leak of TL0 users' websites to anonymous visitors.

findings.title: `User#save` does not update `website_name` from the server response
findings.body: Previously `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving a user's `website` in preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on their profile. Now that `website_name` is computed on the server in `UserSerializer`, `User#save` (lines 206-214) only copies `bio_excerpt` from `data.user` back onto the model (`self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)`). After saving preferences, `model.website_name` on the client remains stale (or `undefined` if a website was newly added) until a full page reload.
